sentences.text: The plaintiff has filed this suit against the defendant for permanent injunction.

2. The case of the plaintiff in brief is as under:
It is contended that, the plaintiff is the absolute owner in possession and enjoyment of the property bearing Site No. 33, Pattanagere City Municipal Council Katha No.
58, Situated Halgevaderahalli, Kengeri Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluk, measuring East to West 40 feet and North to South 60 feet in all measuring 2400 Sq.Ft.
He further contended that one P.J.Joseph has purchased the property on 22/03/1971 through a registered sale deed.
After death of said P.J.Joseph the katha was transferred in the name of his wife Smt. Thangamma, the revenue entries were mutated in her name.
The said Thangamma was died on 20/07/1993 leaving behind her daughter Smt.Nirmala John.
The said Nirmala John executed the GPA in favour of B.T.Bhaskar, Dharmapala.M.K. and V.Krishnamurthy.
After execution of GPA by Smt. Nirmala John, the GPA holders have sold the property in favour of plaintiff through a registered sale deed on 26/06/2000.
After purchase of the property the katha was transferred in the name of plaintiff.
The plaintiff has paid the taxes to BBMP.
After execution of sale deed in favour of the plaintiff he was in possession and enjoyment of the said property.

He further contended that on the northern side of the schedule property there is widening of road and as such the measurement of the property from North to South is diminished by 34 feet on the eastern side and 30 feet on the western side.
Any event there is no reduction of measurement from East to West.
Hence the plaintiff is in peaceful possession of the property.

He further contended that the defendant has no right or whatsoever he is interfering from the eastern side and as such the widening of road on the northern side of the suit schedule property is not of much consequences as far as the defendant is concerned.
The defendant is no way concerned to the property but he has tried to encroach the property of the plaintiff.
3. Plaintiff further contended that during the expansion of road the BBMP has awarded FAR in lieu of compensation to the respective owners in whose property the widening had happened.
The widening had happened through out i.e., the road which runs from East to West.
On the other hand the defendant is no way concerned to the property he has tried to interfere with the property of the plaintiff, therefore the plaintiff has constrained to file the suit.
He prays to grant permanent injunction against the defendant.
4. After institution of the suit, this Court got issued summons to the defendant.

In response to the summons the defendant has appeared through his counsel and filed written statement contending that, the suit of the plaintiff is not maintainable either in law or on the facts and same is liable to be dismissed.
He further contended that, the plaintiff has suppressed the facts and filed the suit.
He has contended that one P.J.Joseph has purchased the property on 22/03/1971 through a registered sale deed and katha was transferred.
After death of said P.J.Joseph the katha was transferred in the name of his wife Smt. Thangamma, the revenue entries were mutated in her name are not within the knowledge of defendant.

He further contended that, Smt.Nirmala John, the daughter of P.J.Joseph Sri. Janardhana Mariyappa vs N.B.Gurudev on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21426567/

As such plaintiff cannot contend that he is in peaceful possession and enjoyment of the suit property as shown in the schedule.

In the Ex.P21 it has not mentioned the boundaries as mentioned in the Ex.P1 nor Ex.P15.
On the other hand plaintiff has not produced any revenue document to prove that his site is coming in Sy. No. 290/1 and 290/2.
Even though the plaintiff has not produced any layout plan nor photos to prove that where his site is situated in the said place.

On the other hand defendant has produced some photos which clearly reflect the Navami apartments and infront of Navami apartment there is a road and there is no vacant site abutting to the Navami apartment.
It is the burden on the plaintiff to prove where his site is situated and defendant site is situated.
On perusal of the said photos it has seen that some portion of property were left out without construction, but on the said vacant space there is a high tension wire is proceeded.
Such being the case plaintiff has not proved that his site is situated in the said place and by the western side the defendant site is situated and tried to interfere in the suit property.
However, the plaintiff has not produced any other independent witness to prove that the defendant is trying to encroach and interfere in the suit property.
In the Ex.P18 even he has not mentioned the boundaries of his site.

Even he has not mentioned in the evidence after acquisition of BBMP he remains 1163 feet for the said remaining portion which site defendant site is situated has not at all mentioned in the Ex.P18 nor in Ex.P15.

When the plaintiff has approached the Court of law stating that defendant is trying to interfere the suit schedule property, then he have to prove by producing proper and reliable evidence that the defendant is trying to interfere in the suit schedule property.
However, PW1 clearly admitted in the evidence that towards eastern side and western side defendant site is not situated.
He further deposed in between the Sy. No. 290/1, 290/2 the survey No. 58 is not coming.

On the other hand defendant has purchased the property in Sy. No. 290/2,
such being the case the plaintiff has failed to prove that the defendant has encroached and interfered in the suit property.
Therefore the plaintiff has failed to prove the interference of defendant.

Hence,
I answer issue No. 2 in the Negative.
26. Issue No. 3:

Counsel for the plaintiff has argued that Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held in ILR 1988 KAR 554 Narasimha Shastry vs Mangesha Devaru "It has been held that where the sale deed mentions the boundaries specifically and clearly to identify the property, the actual extent of the land not being clear, the recitals as to boundary should prevail."

sentences.text: Based on the said judgment the prays to decree the suit of the plaintiff.
With due respect ratio laid down in the said judgment that when there is no clear about the extent then the boundary will prevail.
In the present case the plaintiff has contended that he has purchased the Site No. 33 to an extent of East West 40 feet and North South 60 feet in all 2400 Sq.Ft.
He further deposed that the BBMP has acquired some portion and remaining 1161 Sq.ft stands in the name of plaintiff.
Such being the case it is the plaintiff to prove the boundaries.
He further deposed that the BBMP has acquired the property then he ought to prove the boundaries of the suit property.
Therefore with due respect to the ratio laid down in the above said judgment are not applicable to the present case.

Vasavi Co-operative Housing Society Ltd., and Civil appeal No. 1382/2022 decided on 03/03/2022 by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Prahladji V/s. Manibem Sagmalbai.

O R DE R Suit filed by the plaintiff against the defendant is hereby dismissed with costs.
